title: Premium Prices r baddd
body:
The app is small and only has a little over 500 reviews at the moment.

 Having premium prices this heavy are wrong when the app is that small and not well known. If you want the app to expand, the premium needs to be cheaper or people like myself won’t buy into the app as much as we like it.

- $9.99 a month
- $39.99 per year
- $129.99 life time

Respectfully, the prices are not anywhere close to worth it considering what the premium offers… not saying the premium isn’t good but at those prices it can’t be considered. For example, there are annual plans out there for other apps that are a decent chunk cheaper and offer way more features and functionality for the user. 

Usually on other habit/productivity apps there are subscription slashes on ALL premium plans on special days like new years and even student discounts which I think could be offered to incentivize more people to download this app and help spread the word out!

The app is good but these are just my 2 cents considering the current state of premium subscriptions. Will come back to the app & update my review if anything changes.

title: Good, simple, straightforward
body:
I was inspired to try habit formation by a good friend of mine who introduced me to Seinfeld’s X effect. We normally would make giant poster grids with the largest markers we could find at the craft store. The dopamine hit for crossing out a day where a habit was successfully completed was a really satisfying end to the day. Sadly I moved away from my old town, and I haven’t really had much interest in hanging a big poster in my room that I share with my partner.

Everyday fits the bill for this in many ways. It synchronizes really well, it’s much more discreet than the giant posters, and it is VERY easy to document progress. My one, and only, complaint is that it doesn’t have the same dopamine hit as the posters. It’s close with the flash the icons do once they’re tapped, but something more extreme would be greatly appreciated.

title: Needs more
body:
I really loved this app when I first got it. But after over a month of using I had to switch to the Done app instead. With everyday you can’t see on a calendar which days you did or didn’t complete. You can only go back so far and then it just vanishes. I can’t view my inputted selections from January. Which is really unfortunate since I paid for the yearly membership. And at $40 that’s a steep price to pay for your information to just vanish. I would have preferred to be able to see on a calendar view my progress. Now I’ve paid and I’ve switch to a different developer who can meet the needs I want. And at a significantly lower cost too. $25 for the years and it includes SIX different habit forming apps. 
I wish I could support this app as the colour aspect was what drew me to it. But sadly it’s lacking more.
Response to your reply it does not tell you on a calendar view I mark things off on my calendar as well and when I looked at that block view it didn’t not add up correctly per day going backwards. Your app is lacking in a lot of areas. Take a look at the done app and see just how many features you’re missing. I’m out $40 now for your app that I’ve now deleted cause it’s useless to me but yet Done app gave me SIX different apps full feature for only $25 for the year. You need to rethink you’re extremely overpriced app for a bunch of coloured blocks.
EDIT #2. Maybe because I’m out $40 for an app that only colours squares and doesn’t even track them properly for history. Your history view is WRONG and does not align with my calendar. You’re robbing people. $40 is a damn joke. You should be ashamed of yourself.

title: Great interface and contents
body:
I love how easy it is to gauge every habit organized in one place. Also, the analytical feature is really helpful. Motivating contents are great and I prefer the resources Everyday gives than meditating fictional stories from some other apps. It is just my own preference. 

I’ve tried other popular habit apps yet decide to pick this one and delete the others. 

However, if there is some feedback I could give, it would be to add a time log feature. I find myself not having the patience to track down the time duration of each activity I do. I set habit as hours put in, for example: 30’ reading books. It would be nice at the end of month to know how many hours did I invest in a particular habit, or how many percentage did I really stick to that goal. 

If I can just nitpick one more thing, it is the difficulty to click backwards after I view resources. I had to press many times or press hard somehow. 

Thank you for creating this app. Thanks for spending the time reading my long review as well. Wish you the best!
